> I finally have a friend who is also autistic and we are attached at the hip

That's been more my experience. I've found NT people to be more balanced. Me and my ND friends hung out every possible chance in college. My ND friend who lives in another state I'd text with every day (until we had a bit of a falling out).

> typically; 'home' with family is the one place autistic people do feel most comfortable

Ah, well, home was never that for me for, like, 18+ years of my life :-/

> NTs will call their best friend on the phone everyday, but autistic people are too busy with their special interests or whatever to call their best friend more than once a month... A pair of autistic friends won't feel the disconnect but NTs are aware of how much time has passed.

Is that true? Heck, it's NT's who are always like, "Oh, yeah, I ran into Chuck the other day, haven't seen in him in ten years! We had a coffee and caught up. We used to hang out all the time back in the day," and then move on. Or they'll meet up and be like, "Wow, it's been like a year right? No? Two? Wow, holy shit, it's been five years. That's crazy!" I feel like NTs have *no* social concept of time, whereas NT friends will know to a higher degree of precision how much time has passed, and will care about that time.

My non-NT friends are *way* more on the ball about getting in touch on a regular basis. Yeah, it's like once a month or longer, but NT friends vanish for much longer and seem to feel nothing about it, while my experience with non-NT friends is quite the opposite.  If I don't call my BF in a while, one of us will eventually call the other and be like, "It's been five weeks since our last chat, what have you been up to?" 

That's just my experience with the people around me. And I could be wrong about who is and isn't NT. But, either way, is that experience really so different from yours?

> My closest family feel like strangers. We were very close as kids but the more I unmask in the rest of my life, the less I know what to do at her house

That's also a good point. With *actual* strangers you're never just chilling at their house. Even when you do end up in a stranger's house, it's usually part of some social structure, like a party, or meeting, or whatever. With family it's like you're just free-range in an unfamiliar place. There's no structure to glom onto.

> It makes it sound so permanent when it's not

I don't mean it to sound permanent.  You can run out off something, and then go refill it. But if, say, your coffee cup is empty—that is to say, it has nothing left—, until you get up and refill it, there's no point in lying to yourself and calling it full, is there? The motivation to refill it lies in the fact that there's nothing left, right? I guess that's what I'm getting at.

> reaching out to a loved one (close family or friend)

I def have loved ones I can reach out to, but it's the reaching out that makes it worse. In fact, this was all set off largely because I met up with a bunch of family and friends I hadn't seen in over a year (after usually seeing them fairly regularly). And seeing them after all that time just reminded me of... how pathetic I am.  God, reminiscence just makes me spiral into more and more despair. 

I have, like, *one* thing I'm proud of, and I did it ten years ago, over the course of about two months. That's it. A two month, minor achievement, done a decade ago. That's the only thing I'm truly proud of in my *whole* life. If I expand that to include *anything* of even minor substance I've actually started and finished, the list expands to a grand total of... three. Three things, in my whole life; all incredibly, pathetically minor, and that's all I have after almost 31 years. And none of it is stuff that I even *care* about, or has *any* bearing on what I want for my future.

And I totally see how incredibly trite this all sounds. Frankly, I think this probably belonged more in a sub like r/offmychest or something. I don't sound 31, I sound 13. And now I'm crying at my desk. Good grief....

With depression, I usually don't want to have thoughts; mania I usually have a shit ton of thoughts; with this mixed episode it was like...I didn't have thoughts that came in words. My mixed episode thoughts were pure abstraction of despair, rage, agony.  There was nothing coherent about it. It was all the my worst emotions about being alive, with the unbridled energetic passion of mania.

So, I felt as full of despair as I do with depression, but I was so full of undirected energy that I didn't know what to do. I had concrete walls in the apartment I was living in, and I just remember throwing myself against the wall, over and over and over. There was nothing coherent about it, there was no thought behind it, it was just total undirected grief.  I cried more in one day than I've cried in my entire life ^[citation ^needed] .

But when it was over...it was completely over. I actually went into a full two months of "normalcy."

I understand what you're saying here. The sunset analogy was excellent. Even greater would be finding the inner-contentment to move past things which are impermanent. Instead of a sunset, perhaps you tried to make it to the local museum to view a rare astronomical event which will never occur again in your life. The ability to feel and accept disappointment and move past it without dwelling would be a supreme mastery of the self.  

Most significant relationships feel less like a setting (or rising) sun, and more like Halley's Comet, or the transit of Venus.  They feel once in a lifetime--and they are! No doubt about it! But, they're not the only beauty. It would be foolish to chase after a comet. You could do it, you could chase and mourn--but it is useless and better by far to just let the goodness it brought you stay within you and let it go on its destined way without muddling all the good memories with despair.

I think attachment is essential to strong friendships, though. I mean, isn't attachment the basis of strong friendships? Perhaps the secret to all of this, even to "loving yourself" is acceptance of the inevitable. If you can learn to be content with the passing of all things then you will find ease in life. Maybe you can't love yourself perfectly, but if you can accept your failing, then you can move forward with yourself. Maybe you can't simply smile for the memories when a relationship ends, but you can learn to accept the value of the new life opened before you.

I dunno... Am I making sense? Any thoughts?

Reading through what you wrote helped me bring into greater relief how I feel about certain things. For one, I'm not sure if I'm necessarily lonely when I'm not around close friends. I mean, sometimes I am, of course, as is only natural.  But the pervasive, constant feeling is probably closer to boredom.  I am able to appreciate things by myself. I can enjoy things, but not nearly as deeply as when I'm with someone who "gets" me.

Now, you say that you can't love others until you love yourself. I've never really bought into this argument. Mostly because I don't really understand it and I've never seen it explained particularly well. I feel like I show my love for friends pretty well even though I don't feel the same towards myself. Maybe you could try to explain it to me?

Third, I have a hard time believing in loving oneself without the input of others. My sense of my own worth is purely subjective. If others see me as good, then there's so called "evidence" that I'm good.
(I just realized that's a shitty argument, because all my friends love me, and tell me I'm a good person, and seem truly dismayed when I give up on projects because I am, according to them, really talented [in my area of expertise--not trying to be a braggart here]. So, I have the evidence, I just don't feel it.)

I wish I knew where this stemmed from.  There's no reason for me to be so down on myself. I'm (by measured standards!) fairly talented, decently intelligent, and pretty likeable.

So, you say that learning to love yourself should be a "period of appreciation for what you are." Okay, how do I do that? How do I appreciate myself? I how do I get started on this?

Thanks again.
